items.title: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
items.summary: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.

items.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
items.summary: Amazon wants to be the king of AI cloud computing and become the first $1 trillion revenue business. But to do that it will have to continue on its capex spending spree, its CEO said Thursday.

items.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
items.summary: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.

items.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
items.summary: Rivian doesn't disclose if the value of its $5.8 billion joint venture will expand as a result.

items.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
items.summary: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings is buying ADT in a $15.3 billion deal, with plans to bring AI to the home security business.

items.title: Meta quietly launches an AI fashion app called Style Sketch
items.summary: The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from photos you’ve already shared, or lets you add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a quick video, or uploading images from your camera roll.

items.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now

items.title: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr
items.summary: Uno reverse! After Wispr added meeting notes to its dictation app, Granola is adding dictation to its meeting notetaker. The voice AI wars are getting interesting.

items.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
items.summary: Mistral says its new model can afford organizations a kind of control over its cyber defenses that closed models can't.

items.title: US investigated Chinese spy plot aimed at Nvidia CEO
items.summary: A top executive of a Singapore AI cloud company that was accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China could also have been a Chinese spy, sources have told the New York Times.
